prompts: Remember the little archery games of the Windows 95 days? We want the first level of one, our own, in {WS}/game/index.html, a single file. An archer you aim with the mouse, pulling the bow back for power, balloons to pop, a score on screen, a way to start and a way to lose. How it looks, plays and sounds is your call, and that is what we care about most: a minute of play should be fun, and every shot and hit should feel and sound good. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts, and by playing it.
answers:
[goal] Single-file Win95-style balloon archery game in ./game/index.html.

[action] Built and played it: canvas game, mouse aim, hold-to-charge bow, falling wobbling balloons, particle pops, WebAudio SFX (shoot, pop, miss, game-over, win jingles), score HUD with arrow pips, start screen, lose (arrows out + last balloon escapes) and win (score 100).

[result] Verified live in browser: menu rendered, click started play, charge bar filled while holding, arrow flew with trail, popped a balloon — score 0→5, one pip consumed. Tab closed.

[assumptions] Lose = run out of arrows and let the last balloon escape; win = reach 100 pts (small balloons worth 10, medium 5, big 2); 10 arrows per round; no build step, Google Fonts only (Press Start 2P), all audio synthesized in-browser.

[evidence] Screenshots above show menu, HUD (SCORE 0, 10 pips, TARGET 100), charging, arrow in flight, and SCORE 5 after the pop.
